situation: Postgres up; spool holds 3 new event lines and 1 tickmark
expect: exit 0; 3 events rows and 1 cap_tick row; offset at end of file; last_ship_ok_at set

situation: Docker daemon down
expect: exit non-zero within 30 s; offset unchanged; spool unchanged; the launching tick pass is not slower

situation: the same spool shipped twice
expect: second ship inserts 0 event rows; row counts identical

situation: a snap line older than the row already in Postgres
expect: row unchanged

situation: shipper killed mid-script (psql exit 137)
expect: offset unchanged; next ship resends and equals a single clean ship

situation: a second ship launched while the first runs
expect: second exits 0 immediately without reading the spool

situation: a block_reason holding a token-shaped string
expect: the captured script holds the scrubbed form; the raw string appears nowhere in it

situation: a spool line with v 2 or an unknown t
expect: ship stops before that line, offset left before it, lookout_spool_bad on stderr, exit non-zero

situation: Postgres returns after 2 h down with 240 passes queued
expect: one ship drains in order; final cap_tick equals the newest pass

situation: a spool line this version cannot parse (unknown v/t or an unknown row key)
expect: exit EXIT_SPOOL_BAD (not 3), offset left before the line; a genuine psql SQL error still surfaces psql own exit 3 unchanged, so the two are told apart by return code alone

situation: a backlog larger than CHUNK_ROWS/CHUNK_BYTES
expect: more than one psql call; the offset advances after each chunk lands, not only once at the end; every row ships exactly once

situation: a spool row that parses cleanly but Postgres rejects on a NOT NULL/check/unique/FK constraint
expect: the row moves to the .rejected sidecar with the psql error; the good rows around it still ship; exit 0

situation: a chunk's psql failure carries no SQLSTATE class 22/23 (e.g. 42P10 schema drift)
expect: no row is isolated or quarantined; the real rc surfaces; offset unchanged

situation: a bad prices.json entry fails the whole-chunk attempt; the chunk retried without prices ships clean
expect: nothing is quarantined (never row-shaped); rc 0 and the offset reaches the end; prices_at stays unset so prices retry next run; one stderr line carries the prices error

situation: one row's SQLSTATE is class 22 (data exception, e.g. 22007 invalid timestamp) rather than class 23
expect: that row is quarantined the same as a class-23 constraint violation; the rest of the chunk still ships; exit 0

situation: one row's SQLSTATE has a letter (22P02, invalid_text_representation - a bad int/bool/array through jsonb_populate_record)
expect: that row is quarantined the same as an all-digit code; the rest of the chunk still ships; exit 0

situation: a mixed chunk where one row's own SQLSTATE is systemic (42P10, class 42, real message says "constraint" too)
expect: no isolation/quarantine regardless of the other rows in the chunk; rc is the real psql failure, offset unchanged

situation: every row in the chunk fails with the same recoverable SQLSTATE (23502)
expect: nothing is quarantined (never row-shaped); rc is the real psql failure, offset unchanged

situation: prices AND one row both fail (23502); the chunk is retried once without prices before isolating rows
expect: only the one bad row is quarantined; the good rows ship; prices_at is not updated

situation: a row is quarantined and ship exits 0
expect: one stderr line gives the quarantined count and the .rejected path

situation: prices fail but the prices-free retry ships every row (rc 0)
expect: one stderr line says prices failed and carries the first 300 chars of the psql error
